title: Pipe Tracing System
model_title: Pipe Tracing System (Steam Tracing & Electric Heat Tracing)

introduction.definition: A pipe tracing system supplies heat to a pipe to replace what it loses through its insulation, keeping the product above its freezing, congealing or crystallisation temperature. Steam tracing runs small tubes of steam alongside the pipe, drained by a trap; electric tracing uses a self-regulating heating cable controlled by a thermostat. Both are covered by insulation.
applications: Caustic and liquor lines in alumina refineries
Heavy fuel oil, bitumen and sulphur
Water and instrument lines in freezing climates
key_points: Tracing maintains temperature; it does not heat up cold lines quickly
Steam: trap at each tracer end; electric: earth-leakage protection
Insulation is part of the system

script.narration: This module introduces the Pipe Tracing System.
A pipe tracing system supplies heat to a pipe to replace what it loses through its insulation, keeping the product above its freezing, congealing or crystallisation temperature.
Steam tracing runs small tubes of steam alongside the pipe, drained by a trap; electric tracing uses a self-regulating heating cable controlled by a thermostat.
Both are covered by insulation.
Typical applications include caustic and liquor lines in alumina refineries; heavy fuel oil, bitumen and sulphur; water and instrument lines in freezing climates; viscous chemicals.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Pipe Tracing System works.
Product flows in the process pipe.
Steam flows in the tracer tube and condenses, releasing heat to the pipe.
The tracer trap drains condensate.
Electric cable spiralled on the pipe heats it; its output falls as the pipe warms.
Insulation keeps the heat in.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Pipe Tracing System.
Check product temperature / thermostat.
Survey tracer traps.
Insulation-resistance test of heating circuits.
Watch for line freezing / plugging: product solidifies. Common cause: failed trap, cable fault, wet insulation.
Watch for ground fault trip: circuit trips. Common cause: damaged cable or seals.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
